articles.title: Preview vs render
articles.summary: The live preview is a quick picture to design with and never writes any files. RENDER builds the real paint and spec files and puts them in your iRacing car folder.
articles.what: Two different things share the middle of the window. The LIVE PREVIEW redraws by itself after you change a zone, a colour or a finish, so you can judge the look. RENDER is the slow, full-quality step: it builds the finished paint file and the spec file (the shine map) and copies them where iRacing can load them. iRacing then lights your car with its own sun, shadows and materials and adds its own number and sponsor stamps, so the same colours and patterns show up but the shine is never an exact match for the preview.
when: You changed something and want to see it before spending a full render.
The preview looks stale, blank or stuck.
The car looks a little different in iRacing than in the preview.
how: Change a zone, colour, finish or slider. The LIVE PREVIEW (right of SOURCE) updates by itself after a moment.
If it did not change, press Refresh above the preview (or F5). Refresh stops a stuck preview and starts a new one.
Press Before After to flip between the last preview and the current one and see what your change really did.

Use the strip under the preview (COMBINED, R METAL, G ROUGH, B COAT) to look at the shine itself: brighter red means more metal, darker green means a sharper mirror, darker blue means a glassier clearcoat.
When the look is right, press RENDER. Only RENDER writes files; the preview never touches your iRacing folder.

controls.label: Refresh
controls.effect: Rebuilds the live preview; use it when the picture is stale or blank (F5).

controls.label: Before After
controls.effect: Compares the last preview with the current one.

controls.label: COMBINED / R METAL / G ROUGH / B COAT
controls.effect: Shows the spec map as one picture or as one channel at a time.

tips: Judge shine in the R METAL, G ROUGH and B COAT views, not in the colour preview: the colour view cannot show a mirror.
If the preview ever shows a red bar saying it failed, Shokker is showing the last good picture; press F5 to rebuild it.
pitfalls: Do not expect the preview to match iRacing exactly. Check the real result in iRacing with Ctrl+R after every render.
A change to the spec (shine) only shows in iRacing after a render; the preview cannot reload the sim for you.
aliases: what is the difference between preview and render

deep.heading: Two things in the middle of the window
deep.body: The LIVE PREVIEW redraws by itself after you change a zone, a colour or a finish, so you can judge the look. RENDER is the slow, full-quality step that builds the finished paint file and the spec file and copies them where iRacing can load them. Only RENDER writes files.

deep.heading: Why iRacing never matches exactly
deep.body: iRacing lights your car with its own sun, shadows and materials and adds its own number and sponsor stamps. The same colours and patterns show up, but the shine is never an exact match for the preview.

deep.heading: Reading the shine views
deep.body: The strip under the preview (COMBINED, R METAL, G ROUGH, B COAT) shows the spec map. Brighter red means more metal, darker green means a sharper mirror, darker blue means a glassier clearcoat. Judge shine here, not in the colour view, which cannot show a mirror.

deep.heading: When the preview is stuck
deep.body: Press Refresh above the preview (or F5) to stop a stuck preview and start a new one. A red failure bar means Shokker is showing the last good picture; F5 rebuilds it. Before After flips between the last preview and the current one.

examples.goal: See exactly what a slider did
examples.result: You flip between the two pictures and see only the difference.

examples.goal: Confirm the shine is right
examples.result: You see the roughness directly instead of guessing from colour.

faq.q: Does the preview change my iRacing files?
faq.a: Never. Only RENDER writes files.

faq.q: The preview is blank or stale.
faq.a: Press Refresh or F5.

faq.q: Why does iRacing look a little different?
faq.a: iRacing adds its own lighting and stamps the number and sponsors on top.

faq.q: Do I need to render after changing only the shine?
faq.a: Yes. A spec change shows in iRacing only after a render and Ctrl+R.

mistakes.symptom: You judge shine from the colour preview
mistakes.cause: The colour view cannot show a mirror
mistakes.fix: Look at R METAL, G ROUGH and B COAT.

mistakes.symptom: You expect iRacing to match the preview exactly
mistakes.cause: iRacing uses its own lighting
mistakes.fix: Check the real result in iRacing with Ctrl+R after every render.

protips: Use Before After after every change you doubt. It makes small differences obvious.

articles.title: The Render button and render size (2048 / 1024)
articles.summary: RENDER builds your finished paint and spec files at the size of the template you opened (2048 or 1024 square) and copies them into your iRacing car folder. It stays greyed until a source paint is loaded.
articles.what: RENDER is the big button in the centre of the window (keyboard: Ctrl+R inside Shokker). It builds the paint file and the spec file for the whole car and writes them to the iRacing car folder in the top bar. The size is not a setting: Shokker renders at the size of the template you opened, and iRacing car paints are 2048 by 2048 (or 1024 by 1024). Always open the template for the car you drive and never resize the canvas.
when: Your preview looks right and you want it in iRacing.
You changed a zone and want to see it in the sim.
RENDER will not start and you need to know what is missing.
how: Open your car template: PSD/XCF/ORA for a layered template or TGA/PNG/JPEG for a flat paint, and wait until the RENDER button switches on.
Type your iRacing User ID (Customer ID) and pick your car in iRacing Car Folder at the top.
Turn the template layers (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) OFF in the Layers panel.
Press RENDER. A green Saved bar appears when the files are written.
Switch to iRacing and press Ctrl+R there to reload the car.

controls.label: RENDER
controls.effect: Builds the paint and spec files and writes them to the iRacing car folder (Ctrl+R in Shokker).

controls.label: Render size
controls.effect: Follows the template you opened. Other sizes are ignored by iRacing.

tips: A render usually takes seconds to about a minute. The engine remembers finished zones, so re-rendering after changing one zone is faster than the first render.
The Saved bar has a Show my files button that opens File Explorer on the folder with your paint highlighted.
pitfalls: Ctrl+R means two different things: in Shokker it starts a render, in iRacing it reloads car textures. Press each in its own window.
If RENDER refuses, read the message: it names the first thing missing (paint, User ID, zones, car folder).
Never resize the canvas: iRacing silently shows paint-shop colours for a paint that is not 2048 or 1024 square.

deep.heading: What RENDER needs
deep.body: The button is greyed (it reads OPEN PAINT FIRST or LOADING PAINT) until a source paint is loaded. After that it can be pressed; if the User ID or the zones are not ready, a message names the first missing thing. With no iRacing Car Folder set the render still runs, but the files are not copied where iRacing can see them.

deep.heading: Speed

faq.a: The size of the template you opened, 2048 or 1024 square.

faq.a: Seconds to about a minute. Re-renders after a small change are quicker.

articles.title: Render history and keeping versions
articles.summary: RENDER HISTORY on the top row brings back one of your recent renders and rebuilds its full recipe. Save to keep copies a render into its own folder so the next render cannot overwrite it.
articles.what: Shokker remembers your recent renders as small pictures. Click one and the whole look comes back: zones, finishes and colours. This is separate from Undo History, which steps back through single edits. On disk Shokker keeps only the two newest renders in its own render folder, so anything you want to keep must be copied with Save to keep.
when: You liked an earlier version better.
You want to compare two looks.
You are about to try something risky and want a safe copy of the current render.
how: Open RENDER HISTORY on the top row (the picture icon).
Click a thumbnail: Shokker rebuilds that look completely. Press Gallery in the footer to see all past renders at a larger size.
Press Recent to pick from the last 10 saved renders with their recipes.
After a render, press Save to keep on the recipe card to copy that render into a keep folder.
To share the look, use Share Recipe (a .shokkerrecipe file with a preview) or Save Card PNG for a picture.

Shokker deletes old renders automatically; Deploy Now only works for the two newest.

articles.title: Why a render is slow, and what to do
articles.summary: A normal render takes seconds to about a minute; two minutes or more means something heavy. Fewer zones and simpler stacks always help, and Shokker gives up after 5 minutes.
articles.what: Most render time goes to zones and finishes. Every zone that has its own painted area (a colour region, a layer or a part) uses memory, and about 20 of them is the limit before the preview or render fails. Stacking many spec patterns, huge masks and heavy finishes adds up. The engine caches finished zones, so a re-render after changing one zone is quicker than the first.
when: A render is taking minutes.
The preview is laggy while you edit.
RENDER says a render is already running.
how: Count your zones. Merge zones that share one look into a single zone.
Hide a zone with its eye icon to test whether one finish is the slow one.
Remove spec patterns you do not need; each stacked one costs time.
If a render is stuck, press Terminate when it appears, wait about a minute, then render again.
If one finish is far slower than the rest, use Settings gear then Report a Problem so it can be fixed.

controls.label: Zone limit per render
controls.range: up to 50 zones accepted, about 20 with their own painted area
controls.effect: Past about 20 painted areas the preview and render fail with a memory message.

controls.label: Render timeout
controls.effect: Shokker gives up waiting after 5 minutes.

tips: Fewer zones with a good colour tolerance beat many tiny zones.
The preview re-renders after each change; F5 forces a fresh one.
pitfalls: Terminate only stops Shokker waiting. The engine still finishes and still copies into iRacing, and a new render during that time says render_busy.
Pressing RENDER again and again makes it worse: wait.

deep.body: Seconds to about a minute is normal; two minutes or more means something heavy. Shokker gives up waiting after 5 minutes.

deep.heading: Where the time goes
deep.body: Most time goes to zones and finishes. Every zone with its own painted area (a colour region, a layer or a part) uses memory, and about 20 of them is the limit before the preview or render fails with a memory message. Up to 50 zones are accepted. Stacked spec patterns, huge masks and heavy finishes add up, and the engine caches finished zones, so re-rendering after changing one zone is quicker.

deep.heading: When it is stuck
deep.body: Press Terminate when it appears and wait about a minute. Terminate only stops Shokker waiting; the engine still finishes and still copies into iRacing, and a new render during that time says render_busy. Pressing RENDER again and again makes it worse.

faq.a: Up to 50 are accepted, but about 20 with their own painted area is the limit before failures.

articles.title: Output files: car_num_ID.tga, car_ID.tga and car_spec_ID.tga
articles.summary: Every render writes a paint file and a spec file named with your iRacing User ID. The paint is car_num_ID.tga or car_ID.tga depending on your number switch, and the shine is car_spec_ID.tga.
articles.what: iRacing finds your paint by file name. The ID in the name is your iRacing Customer ID, not your car number. Shokker writes two files per render: the paint (the colours) and the spec file (red = metal, green = roughness, blue = clearcoat, alpha = lighting mask). Extra files such as spec_*.tga, paint_base.tga and ORIGINAL_* backups of files Shokker replaced may also appear in the folder; they are harmless.
when: You are looking in the folder and wonder which file is which.
You need to know which file to upload to Trading Paints.
You see more files than you expected.
how: Open the iRacing car folder with Show my files on the green Saved bar after a render.
Find car_num_<ID>.tga (Custom Number) or car_<ID>.tga (Sim-Stamped Number): that is the paint.
Find car_spec_<ID>.tga: that is the shine (metal, roughness, clearcoat).
Do not rename them. iRacing only loads files with your own ID in the name.

controls.label: car_num_<ID>.tga
controls.effect: The paint, written when Custom Number is on.

controls.label: car_<ID>.tga
controls.effect: The paint, written when Sim-Stamped Number is on.

controls.label: car_spec_<ID>.tga
controls.range: R metal, G roughness, B clearcoat, A mask
controls.effect: The shine file. iRacing builds a .mip from it the first time it loads it.

tips: Shokker saves paints as 24-bit TGA. Only cars with paintable glass need 32-bit with the template glass alpha filled.
pitfalls: Your saved project (.spb or .shokk) is not an iRacing file: only Shokker can open it.
An ID that is not your Customer ID produces files iRacing never loads for you, with no error message.

deep.heading: Two files that matter
deep.body: The paint is car_num_ID.tga (Custom Number) or car_ID.tga (Sim-Stamped Number). The shine is car_spec_ID.tga. The ID is your iRacing Customer ID, not your car number. The spec file is red = metal, green = roughness, blue = clearcoat and alpha = lighting mask.

deep.heading: Format
deep.body: Paints are saved as 24-bit TGA, 2048 or 1024 square. Only cars with paintable glass need 32-bit with the template glass alpha filled. iRacing builds a .mip from the spec the first time it loads it.

deep.heading: Extra files
deep.body: You may also see spec_*.tga, paint_base.tga and ORIGINAL_* backups of files Shokker replaced. They are harmless. Do not rename the main files: iRacing loads only files with your own ID in the name.

faq.a: No. It is your iRacing Customer ID.

faq.a: A backup of a file Shokker replaced. It is harmless.

articles.title: Custom Number vs Sim-Stamped, and Hide Car Numbers
articles.summary: There is no place to type a car number in Shokker. The two switches next to your User ID only choose the file name, and iRacing decides which file it loads from its own Hide Car Numbers setting.
articles.what: Custom Number writes car_num_<ID>.tga: your paint carries its own number, and iRacing loads this file only when Graphics > Hide Car Numbers is ON. Sim-Stamped Number writes car_<ID>.tga: iRacing stamps the number and sponsors on top, and this is the file iRacing loads by default (Hide Car Numbers OFF). The Shokker switch and the iRacing setting must agree, otherwise iRacing finds no file and quietly shows your paint-shop colours. Shokker starts with Custom Number checked, so this mismatch is the most common reason a first paint does not appear.
when: Your paint does not show up in iRacing.
You see your number twice.
You are not sure which switch to pick.
how: Next to iRacing User ID, tick Custom Number or Sim-Stamped Number (only one can be on).
In iRacing open Settings, Graphics, and check Hide Car Numbers: ON loads car_num_<ID>.tga, OFF loads car_<ID>.tga.
Make them agree. If you change Hide Car Numbers in iRacing, restart iRacing.
Not sure which one iRacing wants? Render once in each mode. Both files stay in the folder and iRacing picks the one it needs.
Press Ctrl+R in iRacing to reload.

controls.label: Custom Number
controls.effect: Writes car_num_<ID>.tga; iRacing needs Hide Car Numbers ON.

controls.label: Sim-Stamped Number
controls.effect: Writes car_<ID>.tga; iRacing stamps the number on top.

tips: iRacing updates can switch Hide Car Numbers back; if a paint that worked yesterday vanishes, check it first.
Trading Paints uses the same two names: it calls car_<ID> files Sim-Stamped Number paints and car_num_<ID> files Custom Number paints.
pitfalls: Seeing the number twice means a number-stamp layer of the template was left visible when you rendered.
Shokker cannot read iRacing settings. It cannot warn you that Hide Car Numbers disagrees; you have to look.

articles.title: Where the files go: the iRacing car folder
articles.summary: Shokker copies every render into the iRacing paint folder of the car you chose, which iRacing creates the first time you run that car. The folder must be the car folder itself, not a file.
articles.what: iRacing reads a paint from Documents/iRacing/paint/<car folder>/. The car folder name is the car path with a space instead of the slash, for example stockcars chevyss. Set iRacing Car Folder once in the top bar and every render lands there. If the field is empty, renders are not copied anywhere iRacing can see, except the last car Shokker remembered when Auto-deploy is on.
when: You are setting up for the first time.
You want to know why files are not appearing in iRacing.
You changed to a different car.
how: Run the car once in an iRacing test session so iRacing creates its paint folder.
In Shokker open the car menu next to iRacing Car Folder: it lists the folders iRacing made on this PC, newest first.
Pick YOUR car (newest is not always yours: check the name) or use the folder button to browse.
Render, then press Show my files on the Saved bar to confirm the files are there.

controls.label: iRacing Car Folder
controls.effect: Where finished files are copied after every render.

controls.label: Show my files
controls.effect: Opens File Explorer on the folder with your paint file highlighted.

tips: If Windows keeps Documents in OneDrive, make sure the folder you pick is the one iRacing really uses; File Explorer can show a second, empty Documents folder.
A paint for car A in the folder of car B is ignored.
pitfalls: If you type a folder that does not exist but its parent does, Shokker may save into the parent and still say it worked. A typo in the last word sends files where iRacing never looks.
Pasting a full file path (ending in car_num_..tga) is sorted out by Shokker, but give it the folder.

articles.title: Seeing it in iRacing: Alt+Tab and Ctrl+R
articles.summary: After a render, Alt+Tab to iRacing and press Ctrl+R there (Reload Car Textures). The car flashes white and shows the new files; no restart is needed.
articles.what: iRacing does not watch your paint folder. You tell it to re-read the files with Ctrl+R in a session that has your car. This is iRacing's own key, not a Shokker key. In a replay iRacing does not reload a car that sits in its pit stall, so scrub to a moment when your car is on track. The 3D Car Viewer in My Content reloads a saved paint by itself. A restart is needed only after changing Hide Car Numbers or the 2048 paint textures graphics option.
when: You just rendered and want to see the result.
The car still shows the old paint.
You changed your number setting.
how: Press RENDER in Shokker and wait for the green Saved bar.
Alt+Tab to iRacing, in a test or race session with your car.
Press Ctrl+R. The car flashes white for a moment and then shows the new files.
In a replay, move to a time when your car is not in the pit lane, then press Ctrl+R.
Tweak, render, reload again. That loop is the whole workflow.
tips: Keep iRacing windowed or Alt+Tab quickly; the reload takes a couple of seconds.
If the shine still looks like an old version, see the .mip article.
pitfalls: Pressing Ctrl+R inside Shokker starts a render, not a reload.
No reload helps if iRacing never found a file; check the User ID, the number switch and the car folder first.

articles.title: Auto-deploy and Deploy Now
articles.summary: Setting the iRacing Car Folder is what copies your files into iRacing. Auto-deploy only matters when that folder is empty, and Deploy Now sends the last render to a different car.
articles.what: With a car folder set, every render is copied into it. Auto-deploy after render (Settings gear) is a fallback: when the car folder is empty it copies into the last car Shokker remembered. Under a finished render you will also find Deploy to a different car: pick another car, press Deploy Now, and the same render is also copied into that car's folder. Only the two newest renders are kept, so deploy right away.

You are not sure what Auto-deploy does.
Files are not reaching the folder.
how: Set iRacing Car Folder in the top bar. That is enough for normal use.
Open the Settings gear and tick Auto-deploy after render only if you want the fallback (it starts off).
After a render, open Deploy to a different car on the recipe card.
Choose the other car in Deploy Car Select and press Deploy Now.

articles.title: Trading Paints and .mip files
articles.summary: Trading Paints takes your paint as a TGA or PNG and your spec only as a .mip file that iRacing builds from car_spec_ID.tga. Never upload your saved Shokker project.
articles.what: iRacing never sends textures between drivers; other drivers see your paint only when your files sit in their own paint folder, which is what Trading Paints does. Upload the paint file Shokker rendered (car_num_<ID>.tga or car_<ID>.tga, 2048 or 1024 square). For the shine, drive the car once in an iRacing test session: iRacing compiles car_spec_<ID>.tga into car_spec_<ID>.mip next to it, and that .mip is what Trading Paints wants. Shokker has a Copy TP Desc button for the description text; there is no automatic upload.
when: You want other drivers to see your paint.
Trading Paints says it is the wrong file type.
The shine looks like an old version.
how: Press RENDER, then Show my files on the Saved bar to open the folder.
Upload car_num_<ID>.tga or car_<ID>.tga (the one that matches how you drive) to Trading Paints as the paint.
Load the car once in an iRacing session. iRacing creates car_spec_<ID>.mip.
Upload that .mip as your spec. Trading Paints does not accept the spec as a .tga.
Optional: press Copy TP Desc on the recipe card to paste the finish list into the description.

controls.label: Copy TP Desc
controls.effect: Copies a Trading Paints description with your zone finishes and colours.

tips: Also give your car a plain paint-shop colour scheme in iRacing so drivers without your files do not see a white car.
If the shine still looks old, move car_spec_<ID>.mip out of the folder and press Ctrl+R in iRacing.
pitfalls: The .spb or .shokk file you save is a Shokker project; Trading Paints will refuse it.
The Trading Paints Downloader writes into the same folders with the same names; while testing a local paint, close it or turn off Update My Own Paints.
Custom Number paints need Trading Paints Pro.

articles.title: Photoshop round trip and other exports
articles.summary: Shokker writes TGA files for iRacing, plus optional ZIP, PNG-channel and Photoshop round-trip exports. It opens PSD, XCF and ORA templates but does not write them.
articles.what: The layered formats (PSD, XCF, ORA) are inputs only: you open one with the PSD/XCF/ORA button. For output you have three extras. Export ZIP Package (Settings gear) bundles the paint TGA, spec TGA and a preview into one ZIP after each render. Export to Photoshop (Layers panel > Actions > Photoshop round-trip) writes named TGA exchange files to a folder you choose for editing in Photoshop, and you bring the TGA back afterwards. Channel PNG Export writes the paint and the separated spec channels as PNG pictures for inspection; it does not make final iRacing TGAs.
when: You want to touch up in Photoshop or GIMP.
You want a ZIP to send someone.
You want to look at the spec channels as pictures.
how: For a ZIP: turn on Export ZIP Package in the Settings gear, render, then press Download ZIP Package under the render. Download it right away; it is not kept.
For Photoshop: open the Layers panel, Actions, then Photoshop round-trip. Type a car file name, pick an export folder and press Export.
Edit the exchange files in Photoshop, then bring the TGA back into Shokker (Import TGA in the Settings gear brings in a spec map).
For inspection pictures: ZONES > More > PNG Channels Export, choose a folder, export.

Saving flat TGA to disk from another program does not update Shokker; re-open the file.

articles.title: Saving projects, recipes and reloading later
articles.summary: Save / Open stores your whole workflow (the open paint, every zone and all layer settings) in one file. Recipes (.shokkerrecipe) and SHOKK files are lighter ways to keep or share a look.
articles.what: Three kinds of file keep your work. A project (.spb, from Save / Open) holds the open paint including a PSD, every zone and all layer settings so you can come back later; only Shokker opens it. A recipe (.shokkerrecipe) stores the look (zones, finishes, colours) and can be imported on any car with Import Recipe. A SHOKK file (.shokk, ZONES > More > SAVE SHOKK) stores zones and finishes and, optionally, the paint. None of these are files iRacing or Trading Paints can use; they are for you and for sharing.
when: You will continue tomorrow.
You want to send a look to a friend.
You want a backup before experimenting.
how: Press Save / Open on the top toolbar and choose to save. Name the project.
Come back later with Save / Open and load it. Check your iRacing User ID and car folder afterwards: loading someone else's file can overwrite them.
To share a look, press Share Recipe on the render card, or save a .shokk with a name, an optional author and a short description.
To use a shared look, press Import Recipe and choose the .shokkerrecipe file.
If Shokker says Autosave is off for a big design, save an SPB project now.
